item.title: Ella Langley, Morgan Wallen & More: Inside Country Music’s Historic Decade and What’s To Expect Next
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our show, where we dive into the latest trends in music. Today, we're talking about the country music boom of the 2020s. Join me as we explore the artists and albums that are making history.
[Music transitions]
Host: Country star Ella Langley has been smashing records with her music. Her second album, Dandelion, debuted at number one on the Billboard 200 and Top Country Albums charts. But that's not all - she's also made history with her single "Choosin' Texas", which became the first song by a woman to simultaneously hit number one on the Billboard Hot 100, Hot Country Songs, and Country Airplay charts.
[Short music clip]
Host: Langley's not the only one making waves in country music. Megan Moroney's album Cloud 9 also reached number one on the Billboard 200 chart, making her and Langley the first women to top the chart with country music. And with artists like Morgan Wallen and Kacey Musgraves also releasing hit albums, it's clear that country music is experiencing a commercial boom.
[Music transitions]
Host: Langley's album Dandelion has remained at number one on the Top Country Albums chart for five consecutive weeks, setting a modern-era record. And her single "Choosin' Texas" has ruled the Hot Country Songs chart for 26 weeks. But that's not all - she's also become the first artist to occupy the top two spots on the Hot 100 chart for multiple weeks with her songs "Choosin' Texas" and "Be Her".
[Short music clip]
Host: Morgan Wallen has also been leading the charge for country music's record-shattering run. His album Dangerous: The Double Album spent 97 weeks at number one on the Top Country Albums chart, and his subsequent albums have also broken records. And with country music's streaming numbers reaching new highs - 1.24 billion on-demand audio streams in 2020 - it's clear that the genre is experiencing a surge in popularity.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for today's show. Thanks for joining me as we explored the country music boom of the 2020s. Until next time, keep listening to the music that's making history.
